frequency_question: How often do states successfully establish domestic production of advanced guided weapons within 28 months of initial foreign supply?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign states engaged in active major conflict that received foreign cruise/tactical missiles and attempted domestic manufacturing/assembly lines. Excludes standard small arms, basic artillery, and unguided munitions.

cases.name: Taiwan Hsiung Feng missile development with US/foreign tech assistance (1970s)
Pakistan Babur cruise missile development via reverse engineering/foreign assistance
Iran Noor/Qader cruise missile production derived from Chinese C-802
Ukraine Neptune anti-ship missile domestic series production setup post-2014
Ukraine Vilkha rocket system domestic production scaling post-2018
Georgia domestic production attempt of precision ordnance post-2008

coverage_note: 6 named; believed roughly 7 in total globally since 1970
known_gaps: Classified bilateral defense arrangements regarding deep tech transfers are occasionally opaque.
skeleton: 6 enumerated historical instances of state attempts at domestic advanced missile production during conflict or severe security pressure
validity_reason: Industrial base adaptation rates and technological diffusion speed remain stable across decades of modern missile development.
